steps.instruction: Stay calm and restrain your dog gently to prevent biting.
Open the dog's mouth carefully and look for the foreign object.
If visible, try to remove the object with tweezers. Do not push it further in.
If the object cannot be removed, perform the Heimlich maneuver by placing your fist below the rib cage.
Seek immediate veterinary attention even if the object is removed.

Apply direct pressure to the wound using a clean cloth or gauze.
Maintain pressure for at least 5 minutes without lifting the cloth.
If bleeding soaks through, add more gauze on top without removing the first layer.
Once bleeding slows, gently clean the wound with saline solution.
Transport your dog to the vet for further treatment.
Move your dog to a cool, shaded area immediately.
Apply cool (not cold) water to the body, focusing on the neck, armpits, and groin.
Place wet towels on the dog and use a fan if available.
Offer small amounts of cool water to drink. Do not force water.
Transport to a veterinary clinic as heatstroke can cause organ damage.
Wrap the cat in a towel to restrain safely, leaving the head exposed.
Gently open the mouth and check for visible foreign objects.
If you can see the object, carefully remove it with tweezers or small pliers.
If the cat is unconscious, hold it upside down by the hips and gently shake to dislodge the object.
Visit the vet immediately, even if the object has been removed.
Identify the toxic substance if possible and note the amount ingested.
Do NOT induce vomiting unless specifically instructed by a vet.
Collect a sample of the substance or its packaging for the vet.
Call your veterinarian or animal poison control immediately.
Transport your cat to the vet as quickly as possible.
Check if your rabbit has stopped eating, drinking, or producing droppings.
Gently massage the rabbit's abdomen in circular motions to encourage gut movement.
Offer fresh hay and water. Try syringe-feeding water if the rabbit refuses to drink.
Keep the rabbit warm and encourage gentle movement or exercise.
Seek veterinary care urgently. GI stasis can be fatal within 24 hours.
Isolate the hamster from other hamsters to prevent spreading.
Keep the hamster warm and in a quiet, stress-free environment.
Offer fresh water using a syringe dropper to prevent dehydration.
Clean the cage thoroughly and replace all bedding.
Visit a vet immediately. Wet tail is a serious condition that requires antibiotics.
